vro.config.title: VRO settings
vro.config.dialog.default.title: Reset every VRO setting?
vro.config.dialog.default.message: Every VRO setting, including Diagnostics and the built-in ImmediatelyFast options, goes back to its shipped default and is saved and applied at once. Unsaved changes on this screen are discarded.
vro.config.dialog.experimental.title: Turn on experimental settings?
vro.config.dialog.experimental.message:
These settings ship turned off. They will be turned on, saved and applied at once:
%s
Diagnostics and GPU rendering switches are not changed. Unsaved changes on this screen are discarded.
vro.config.dialog.experimental.none: Every experimental setting is already on.
vro.config.dialog.restart.title: Restart needed
vro.config.dialog.restart.message:
These changes take effect after you restart the game:
%s
vro.config.dialog.restart.message.arena:
These changes take effect after you restart the game (the two buffer-arena sizes after rejoining a world):
%s
vro.config.message.cloth_missing: VRO's settings screen needs Cloth Config. You can still change every setting in config/vault_render_optimization-client.toml or with /vro commands.
vro.config.message.cloth_incompatible: VRO's settings screen does not work with this Cloth Config version. You can still change every setting in config/vault_render_optimization-client.toml or with /vro commands.
vro.config.button.report_bug.summary: Shows the report first; nothing is uploaded or sent by VRO.
vro.config.button.report_bug.tooltip: Opens a preview of a GitHub issue with your versions, rendering mods, changed VRO settings and GPU path status, plus the newest crash report if there is one. Your user folder, name and UUID are removed first. VRO uploads nothing: it can copy the crash report to your clipboard and open the issue page in your browser, and you submit it yourself.
vro.config.button.gpu_benchmark.summary: Tests GPU against CPU rendering on your PC (about 5 minutes) and suggests which GPU switches to use.
vro.config.button.gpu_benchmark.tooltip: Measures every GPU switch on and off in a crowd of mobs, armour stands and items that only you can see, then shows which switches make your game faster. Before you start, stand somewhere safe, above a flat open area, facing empty space: the crowd appears in front of you. The test takes about 5 minutes (up to 7 with a shader pack), and you cannot move or look around until it ends. Opening a menu pauses it. It works on servers where you are not an operator. Your settings change only if you choose Apply at the end.
vro.benchmark.confirm.title: Run the GPU benchmark?
vro.benchmark.confirm.message:
This takes about 5 minutes (up to 7 with a shader pack). You cannot move or look around until it ends.

Stand somewhere safe, above a flat open area, facing empty space: a crowd of mobs and items that only you can see appears in front of you.

Esc pauses the test; /vro benchmark gpu cancel stops it. Nothing changes unless you choose Apply at the end. Unsaved changes on the settings screen are discarded.
vro.benchmark.confirm.no_world: Join a world first: the benchmark runs where you are standing.
vro.benchmark.result.title: GPU benchmark finished
vro.benchmark.result.none: Your current GPU settings are already the fastest on this PC. Nothing was changed.
vro.benchmark.result.changes: These changes made the game faster on your PC:
vro.bugreport.title: Report a VRO bug
vro.bugreport.issue_heading: Issue text that opens on GitHub (personal paths and your name are removed):
vro.bugreport.crash_heading: Crash report that will be copied to your clipboard (%s):
vro.bugreport.status.hint: Nothing is uploaded. Scroll to read everything; you submit the issue yourself on GitHub.
vro.config.gpu.gpu_entity_models.summary: Builds mob and armor model shapes on the graphics card. Off by default; the GPU benchmark below can recommend it.
vro.config.gpu.gpu_entity_models.tooltip: Moves the work of building entity model vertices from the CPU to the graphics card. The draw itself is unchanged, and a startup self-test checks the result matches vanilla exactly. It needs OpenGL 4.3. It pauses on its own when an Oculus shader pack is on (see "GPU models with shaders"), in Compare Mode, or when its checks fail. Turn it off if mobs or items look wrong. Off by default; the GPU benchmark below can recommend it.
vro.config.gpu.gpu_particles.summary: Builds ordinary particle shapes on the graphics card. Off by default; the GPU benchmark below can recommend it.
vro.config.gpu.gpu_particles.tooltip: Uses the same graphics-card path to build ordinary billboard particles. Every particle is still drawn, and unusual particles stay on the CPU. It only works while "GPU entity models" is active and has its own startup self-test. Off by default; the GPU benchmark below can recommend it.
vro.config.gpu.gpu_items.summary: Builds items on the ground, in frames and in hands on the GPU. Off by default; the GPU benchmark below can recommend it.
vro.config.gpu.gpu_items.tooltip: Items on the ground, in item frames, held in hands and on armor stands are built on the graphics card, matching the normal item renderer exactly. This covers block items and flat items such as gems, loot and tools. Whole block models drawn by block entities use the same path. Enchanted (glinting) and custom-rendered items stay on the CPU. It only works while "GPU entity models" is active. Off by default; the GPU benchmark below can recommend it.
vro.config.gpu.gpu_entity_models_with_sh: Keeps GPU models and particles on with an Oculus shader pack.

Experimental, mainly for slower CPUs. With an Oculus shader pack on, entity models and particles stay on the graphics-card path, which writes the extra data Oculus needs. Shader packs usually make the graphics card the bottleneck already, so this extra GPU work can cost more frame time than it saves. Leave it off unless your CPU is the limit.
vro.config.gpu.gpu_particles_with_shader: Keeps only GPU particles on with an Oculus shader pack.

With an Oculus shader pack on, keeps particles on the graphics-card path while mob models go back to the CPU. Particles keep their normal format under shader packs, so they need no extra shader work. "GPU models with shaders" already includes this.
vro.config.chunks.defer_updates.summary: Rebuilds changed chunks in the background to reduce stutter.
vro.config.chunks.defer_updates.tooltip: Asks the renderer to rebuild changed chunks in the background, so the game waits less on them. Under heavy load, placed or broken blocks can take a moment longer to show. It works with vanilla, Embeddium and Rubidium. When off, your renderer's own setting decides.
vro.config.chunks.index_only_sorting.sum: Re-sorts water and glass without re-uploading their shapes.
vro.config.chunks.index_only_sorting.too: When see-through terrain (water, glass, ice) is re-sorted as you move, only the new drawing order is uploaded and the shapes are reused. It works only on checked Embeddium versions. Vanilla and Rubidium are unaffected. Turn it off if see-through blocks flicker or draw in the wrong order.
vro.config.chunks.sort_geometry_cache.su: Experimental: remembers see-through shapes for faster sorting.
vro.config.chunks.sort_geometry_cache.to: Experimental. Keeps the triangle centres of see-through terrain (at most 16 MiB) so re-sorting skips recomputing them. It needs "Faster see-through sorting" on a checked Embeddium version. It is off by default until it has been checked in game with water, glass and shaders.
vro.config.chunks.adaptive_budget_v2.sum: Spreads terrain rebuild uploads across frames based on cost.
vro.config.chunks.adaptive_budget_v2.too: Experimental but on by default. It measures how long terrain uploads take and spreads updates to already-loaded terrain across frames. First-time terrain loading and large backlogs still use the renderer's normal speed. It needs a checked Embeddium version and "Background chunk updates". Turning it off during a backlog can cause one short catch-up hitch.
vro.config.chunks.vertical_enabled.summa: Skips drawing terrain far above or below you.
vro.config.chunks.vertical_enabled.toolt: Terrain sections farther above or below the camera than "Vertical draw distance" are not drawn. Chunks stay loaded and nothing in the world changes. Turn it off if you need to see deep caves or tall builds from far away. It steps aside when Better Fps - Render Distance is installed.
vro.config.chunks.vertical_distance.summ: How far up and down terrain is drawn, in 16-block sections.
vro.config.chunks.vertical_distance.tool: Terrain sections are drawn up to this many 16-block sections above and below the camera. The default of 12 is 192 blocks each way. Lower values draw less terrain, and you may see it end above or below you. It only matters while "Vertical draw limit" is on.
vro.config.chunks.horizontal_enabled.sum: Draws terrain only within a circle around you.
vro.config.chunks.horizontal_enabled.too: Terrain sections beyond a circular radius ("Horizontal draw distance") are not drawn. Chunks stay loaded and nothing in the world changes. It is off by default so your normal render distance is kept. With it on, terrain can visibly end before your render distance.
vro.config.chunks.horizontal_distance.su: Radius of the round draw limit, in 16-block sections.
vro.config.chunks.horizontal_distance.to: Terrain is drawn within this many 16-block sections around the camera. It only matters while "Round horizontal draw limit" is on. A value above your render distance has no visible effect.
vro.config.entities.particle_collision_c: Particles reuse block collision shapes within one tick.

Particles still bounce off and land on blocks exactly as in vanilla. The block shapes they test against are read once per tick instead of once per particle. Every particle still collides. It steps aside when Particle Core or Flerovium is installed.
vro.config.entities.particle_light_cache: Reuses a particle's light value within one game tick.
A particle's brightness is looked up once per game tick instead of every frame. Lighting looks the same. It steps aside when Particle Core or Flerovium is installed.
vro.config.entities.particle_shared_ligh: Particles in the same block share one light lookup per tick.

Particles inside the same block share one brightness lookup for the current tick. The cache has a size limit and is cleared every tick and on world change. It works together with "Particle light cache".
vro.config.entities.particle_billboard_f: Builds flat particle squares with less math per particle.
Builds the four corners of ordinary flat particles directly from the camera direction instead of rotating each corner. Particles look the same. Particles with their own custom drawing are unchanged.
vro.config.entities.particle_billboard_o: Chooses who builds flat particles: Auto, your renderer, or VRO.

Auto uses VRO's particle math with Embeddium/Rubidium's fast writer when available. Renderer hands the whole job to Embeddium/Rubidium (or VRO if neither is installed). VRO always uses VRO's own path. Flerovium takes over when installed, whatever you pick here.
vro.config.entities.skip_empty_particle_: Skips particle draw setup when there are no particles at all.
When there are no particles at all, the particle drawing setup is skipped for that frame. Nothing changes when particles exist. It steps aside when BadOptimizations is installed.
vro.config.entities.particle_tick_compac: Removes expired particles in one pass each tick.

Particles that have finished their lifetime are cleared in one ordered pass instead of one at a time. Every particle still updates in the normal order. It steps aside when Particle Core, Flerovium or AsyncParticles is installed.
vro.config.entities.particle_shared_rand: Particles reuse a random generator instead of making new ones.

New particles reuse a random-number generator (one per thread) that uses Java's normal random method, instead of each making its own. Particle spread and motion have the same randomness as before. It steps aside when Particle Core, Flerovium or AsyncParticles is installed.
vro.config.entities.particle_provider_ca: Looks up how to create each particle type once.

Each particle type's factory is found once and remembered, instead of being looked up again for every spawned particle. The cache is cleared when particle types are registered again. It steps aside when Particle Core, Flerovium or AsyncParticles is installed.
vro.config.entities.allocation_free_frus: Checks if things are on screen without creating temporary objects.

The check that decides whether a mob, block entity or particle is inside your view runs without creating temporary objects. It does the same calculation in the same order, so the answer is identical to vanilla.
vro.config.entities.entity_renderer_cach: Remembers which renderer draws each mob type.

Each mob type remembers its renderer instead of looking it up every time it is drawn. Players are not affected. The cache is rebuilt when resource packs reload. It steps aside when BadOptimizations is installed.
vro.config.entities.block_entity_rendere: Remembers which renderer draws each chest, sign, etc.

Each block entity type (chests, signs, machines) remembers its renderer instead of looking it up every time. The cache is rebuilt when resource packs reload. It steps aside when BadOptimizations is installed.
vro.config.interface.hud_text_geometry.s: Experimental: reuses unchanged plain HUD text between frames.
vro.config.interface.hud_text_geometry.t: Experimental. The letter shapes of plain, unchanged HUD text are reused, and the text is still drawn every frame. Coloured, formatted, animated or custom-font text uses the normal path. It is off until checked in game and steps aside when ImmediatelyFast, Modern UI, Exordium or Smooth Font handles text.
vro.config.interface.skip_empty_toast_re: Skips pop-up (toast) drawing when none are showing.
When no advancement, recipe or other pop-up is queued or visible, its drawing work is skipped. Pop-ups show normally when they exist. It steps aside when BadOptimizations is installed.
vro.config.interface.skip_empty_debug_re: Skips debug overlay drawing when none are turned on.
When no supported debug overlay (for example chunk borders) is on, its drawing work is skipped. It does not affect the F3 screen. It steps aside when BadOptimizations is installed.
vro.config.interface.skip_inactive_tutor: Skips the finished tutorial's empty work each tick.
After the tutorial is done, its empty per-tick update is skipped while no tutorial pop-up is timed. Tutorial hints still work when active. It steps aside when BadOptimizations is installed.
vro.config.compat.farsight_chunk_bound.s: Frees far-away chunks Farsight would otherwise keep forever.
vro.config.compat.farsight_chunk_bound.t: Only when Farsight is installed. Farsight keeps every chunk you have passed in memory until you change dimension. Once a second, this frees chunks the server has already unloaded that are beyond your render distance plus one. Chunks inside render distance stay. This is a memory-leak fix, so Compare Mode does not affect it, and turning it off lets memory grow while you travel.
vro.config.compat.fastload_frustum_bypas: Skips Fastload's unused hook in on-screen checks during play.

Only when Fastload is installed. After the world has loaded, Fastload's hook in the on-screen check has nothing listening, so VRO skips it. Results are the same. It only applies when Fastload's hook is the only change to that check.
vro.config.compat.create_skip_empty_cont: Skips a buffer flush for contraptions with no special blocks.
Only when Create is installed. A moving contraption with no special blocks to draw (chests, signs and the like) skips flushing the shared render buffers. Contraptions look the same.
vro.config.compat.create_contraption_blo: Skips special blocks on contraptions that are off screen.
Only when Create is installed. Special blocks riding on a visible contraption are not drawn when they are outside your view. Anything on screen is drawn as normal.
vro.config.compat.create_contraption_act: Skips drills, saws, etc. on contraptions when off screen.
Only when Create is installed. Moving tools on a visible contraption (drills, saws, harvesters) are not drawn when they are outside your view. Anything on screen is drawn as normal.
vro.config.compat.create_sectioned_contr: Splits big contraptions into 16-block pieces for on-screen checks.

Only when Create is installed. Large contraptions are split into 16-block pieces so parts outside your view are not drawn. Detail, textures and lighting are unchanged. A large contraption may take slightly longer to prepare the first time.
vro.config.compat.create_sectioned_mesh_: Blocks a contraption needs before it is split into pieces.
Only when Create is installed. Contraptions with at least this many visible blocks use "Split large contraptions". Lower values split smaller contraptions too.
vro.config.compat.create_smart_machinery: Uses tighter on-screen bounds for belts, arms and similar machines.

Only when Create is installed. Belts, mechanical arms, deployers, portable storage interfaces and rollers use tighter, direction-aware bounds, so they are skipped sooner once fully off screen. Turn it off if one of these machines pops out of view at screen edges.
vro.config.compat.create_auto_enable_fly: Turns on Flywheel instancing for this session if the pack has it off.

Only when Create is installed. Turns on Flywheel's instancing renderer for this session when the pack has it set to off. Flywheel's own config file is never changed; turning this off returns to the pack's setting immediately. Graphics cards or shader setups that cannot use instancing still fall back safely.
vro.config.compat.create_flywheel_shader: Keeps Create's fast contraption rendering on with Oculus shaders.

Only with Create, Flywheel 0.6.11, Oculus 1.6.x and Embeddium or Rubidium. Normally Flywheel stops its fast GPU path when a shader pack is on. This keeps that path available inside the shader pack. Unsupported setups ignore it, and Create falls back to its normal renderer if anything fails.
vro.config.compat.storage_front_display_: Skips barrel front displays facing away or covered by a block.

Only with the supported Sophisticated Storage version. A barrel's front display (item, count, fill bar, upgrades) is not drawn when it faces away from you or a block sits right in front of it. Visible displays are unchanged.
vro.config.compat.storage_quantity_text_: Reuses limited-barrel count text until the number changes.

Only with the supported Sophisticated Storage version. Limited barrels reuse the formatted count text and its letter shapes until the count changes. Colour and lighting are still applied fresh. The cache has a size limit and is cleared when resource packs reload.
vro.config.compat.storage_fill_level_fas: Draws limited-barrel fill bars without temporary objects.
Only with the supported Sophisticated Storage version. Limited-barrel fill bars are drawn without creating temporary objects. Fill amount, texture, lighting and transparency are unchanged.
vro.config.compat.storage_count_only_ren: Barrel count changes no longer rebuild the surrounding chunk.

Only with the supported Sophisticated Storage version. When only a barrel's count or fill level changes, the surrounding terrain is not rebuilt. Changes that affect the barrel's model still rebuild right away.
vro.config.compat.backport_chunk_meshing: Reuses lookups while building terrain chunk shapes.

Building terrain chunk shapes reuses one block iterator and skips a repeated block lookup. It is not used with Fluidlogged. VRO steps aside when ModernFix or VH Accelerator already does this. Needs a restart.
vro.config.compat.backport_buffer_builde: Stops render buffers from being allocated twice.

Fixes a vanilla bug that allocates the main render buffers twice and wastes memory. It is not used with Isometric Renders or Cracker's Wither Storm Mod. VRO steps aside when ModernFix or VH Accelerator already does this. Needs a restart.
vro.config.compat.backport_entity_model_: Shares identical model cubes to save memory.
Identical cubes in mob models are stored once and shared, saving memory. The cache is cleared when models reload. VRO steps aside when ModernFix or VH Accelerator already does this. Needs a restart.
vro.config.compat.backport_profile_textu: Remembers player skin texture lookups for a short time.

Repeated player skin texture lookups are remembered (up to 2,048 entries, each expiring 60 seconds after its last use). VRO steps aside when ModernFix or VH Accelerator already does this. Needs a restart.
vro.config.compat.backport_model_selecto: Caches multi-part block model rules while loading models.
Rules that pick parts of multi-part block models (such as fences and walls) are cached while models load. VRO steps aside when ModernFix or VH Accelerator already does this. Needs a restart.
vro.config.compat.backport_model_variant: Uses fewer temporary objects when loading block model variants.
Loading block model variants creates fewer temporary objects. Missing-texture reports are kept. VRO steps aside when ModernFix or VH Accelerator already does this. Needs a restart.
vro.config.compat.backport_model_transfo: Remembers model rotation hashes instead of recomputing them.
Model rotation and scale values never change, so their lookup hashes are calculated once and remembered. VRO steps aside when ModernFix or VH Accelerator already does this. Needs a restart.
vro.config.compat.backport_obj_model_cac: Makes Forge's OBJ model caches safe for parallel loading.

Forge's caches for OBJ-format models become safe to use from several threads at once, which avoids rare loading crashes. VRO steps aside when ModernFix or VH Accelerator already does this. Needs a restart.
vro.config.compat.backport_faster_textur: Packs large texture atlases faster while resources load.

Large texture atlases (100 or more textures) are packed with a faster method while resources load. Smaller or unusual atlases use vanilla packing. VRO steps aside when ModernFix or VH Accelerator already does this. Needs a restart.
vro.config.compat.backport_model_data_ma: Fixes a Forge model-data threading bug that can crash.
Fixes a Forge threading bug when block model data refreshes. With old Rubidium and no Embeddium, it is not used. VRO steps aside when ModernFix or VH Accelerator already does this. Needs a restart.
vro.config.compat.backport_ctm_metadata_: Fixes a ConnectedTexturesMod cache threading bug.
Fixes a threading bug in ConnectedTexturesMod's texture-data cache. It applies only to CTM 1.18.2-1.1.5+5. VRO steps aside when ModernFix or VH Accelerator already does this. Needs a restart.
vro.config.compat.transfer_adjacent_bloc: Fixes hidden-face checks next to custom blocks.

Only on supported Embeddium or Rubidium. Fixes how the renderer decides which block faces are hidden by a neighbour, which matters for some custom blocks. It is a correctness fix and stays on in Compare Mode. Needs a restart.
vro.config.compat.transfer_null_buffer_v: Prevents a renderer crash when a buffer is missing while loading.

Only on supported Embeddium or Rubidium. Stops the renderer's fast vertex writer from crashing when its buffer is missing during loading or dimension changes. It is a correctness fix and stays on in Compare Mode. Needs a restart.
vro.config.compat.transfer_direct_ccl_re: Finds CodeChickenLib block renderers directly, not by scanning.

Only on supported Embeddium (not Rubidium) with CodeChickenLib installed. Custom CodeChickenLib block and fluid renderers are found directly instead of scanning the full list each time. Needs a restart.
vro.config.compat.transfer_vertex_buffer: Trims oversized chunk-building buffers so memory does not pile up.

Only on supported Embeddium or Rubidium. Chunk-building buffers that grew for one unusually large chunk are trimmed back (see "Buffer size limit") so long sessions do not keep that memory. Needs a restart.
vro.config.compat.transfer_async_arena_g: Grows terrain video memory in larger, capped steps.

Only on supported Embeddium or Rubidium. When terrain needs more video memory, it grows by a fixed, capped step so it resizes less often. See "Growth step divisor" and "Max extra video memory". Needs a restart.
vro.config.compat.transfer_smooth_fluid_: Keeps smooth lighting on water and other non-glowing fluids.
Only on supported Embeddium or Rubidium. Non-glowing fluids such as water keep smooth lighting, and the lighting choice is cached until resources reload. Needs a restart.
vro.config.compat.transfer_chunk_layer_c: Resets a leftover shader tint after terrain is drawn.

Only on supported Embeddium or Rubidium. Resets the shader colour after each terrain layer so a leftover tint cannot carry over to other things drawn later. It is a correctness fix and stays on in Compare Mode. Needs a restart.
vro.config.compat.transfer_chunk_rebuild: Skips repeat rebuilds of a chunk that is already queued.

Only on supported Embeddium or Rubidium. If a chunk is already waiting to be rebuilt, another request for the same chunk is merged into it, keeping the more urgent one. No update is lost. Needs a restart.
vro.config.compat.vertex_buffer_max_reta: Largest size one chunk-building buffer keeps between builds.

Used by "Limit chunk buffer memory". A buffer larger than this is trimmed back when it next starts a build. The default of 16 MiB suits most packs. Higher values keep more memory for fewer reallocations.
vro.config.compat.vertex_buffer_adaptive: Experimental: trims chunk buffers based on recent use.

Experimental. Chunk-building buffers shrink to what they needed over the last 30 seconds, but only when they start their next build. An idle buffer keeps its memory until it is used again. It needs "Limit chunk buffer memory" active and is off until checked in game.
vro.config.compat.vertex_buffer_aggregat: Extra buffer memory in total before trimming gets stricter.

Used by "Adaptive buffer trimming". Above this total of extra chunk-buffer memory, buffers trim earlier at their next build. It is a soft threshold, not a hard memory cap. Memory needed for a build is never refused.
vro.config.compat.async_arena_growth_div: Smaller = bigger memory growth steps, fewer resizes.

Used by "Steadier terrain memory growth". Each growth step is about the buffer's starting size divided by this number. Smaller values reserve more video memory up front in exchange for fewer resizes. New values apply to terrain buffers created after the change, for example after rejoining a world.
vro.config.compat.async_arena_max_headro: Caps the extra video memory reserved by one growth step.

Used by "Steadier terrain memory growth". This limits only the extra room reserved ahead of time. Memory actually needed for an upload is never capped. New values apply to terrain buffers created after the change, for example after rejoining a world.
vro.config.immediatelyfast.enabled.summa: Turns VRO's built-in copy of ImmediatelyFast on or off.
vro.config.immediatelyfast.enabled.toolt: Groups many small draws (HUD, text, items, maps) into fewer, larger ones. It switches itself off when the standalone ImmediatelyFast mod is installed, or when your Oculus build lacks what it needs. Needs a restart.
vro.config.immediatelyfast.font_atlas_re: Uses larger font textures so text needs fewer texture swaps.
Font glyphs are packed into larger textures, so drawing text switches textures less often. Needs a restart.
vro.config.immediatelyfast.map_atlas_gen: Puts many maps into one shared texture.
Maps (in item frames or held) share one large texture instead of one texture each, which helps in rooms with many maps. Needs a restart.
Draws HUD text, bars and icons in fewer batches.
HUD text, boxes, item icons and overlays are collected and drawn in fewer batches. While this or fast text lookup is active, VRO's own "Reuse HUD text shapes" steps aside. Needs a restart.
vro.config.immediatelyfast.fast_text_loo: Finds each letter's font data faster when drawing text.
Speeds up finding the font data for each character drawn. Text looks the same. Needs a restart.
vro.config.immediatelyfast.fast_buffer_u: Reuses graphics buffers when uploading drawn shapes.
Reuses graphics memory when uploading drawn shapes, instead of reallocating it every time. Needs a restart.
vro.config.immediatelyfast.experimental_: Experimental: batches hotbar item drawing too.
Experimental. Hotbar items are also drawn in batches. ImmediatelyFast warns this can cause visual glitches. It only works while HUD batching is on. Needs a restart.
vro.config.updates.check_for_updates.sum: Checks VRO's update list online and tells you about new versions.
vro.config.updates.check_for_updates.too: Downloads VRO's small update list from GitHub in the background and can show a notice on the main menu and in chat. VRO never downloads or installs updates itself. Turn it off to stop the check and hide all notices.
vro.config.updates.update_types.summary: Critical only, or all new versions.
vro.config.updates.update_types.tooltip: Critical shows only updates marked critical. All also shows normal updates. Reminders repeat at most every 5 launches (critical) or 10 launches (normal).
vro.config.diagnostics.compare_mode.summ: Turns off VRO's speed-ups so you can compare with and without.
vro.config.diagnostics.compare_mode.tool: Turns off VRO's performance features so you can measure the difference. Crash guards, cleanup, the Farsight memory limit and some correctness fixes stay on. Most features switch at once, but ModernFix backports and Embeddium transfers only follow this after a restart. Remember to turn it off afterwards.
vro.config.diagnostics.particle_diagnost: Collects particle timing and cache counters for /vro particles.
Records particle counts, timings and cache hits for /vro particles status. Collecting these costs a little time itself, so leave it off for normal play.
vro.config.diagnostics.storage_diagnosti: Collects barrel render counters for /vro storage.
Only with the supported Sophisticated Storage version. Records barrel display and cache counters for /vro storage. Collecting them adds a little work, so leave it off for normal play.
vro.config.diagnostics.immediatelyfast_d: Hides ImmediatelyFast's buffer-pool line on the F3 screen.
Cosmetic only. It stops ImmediatelyFast from adding its "Buffer Pool" lines to the F3 debug screen. It does not change performance. Needs a restart.
For troubleshooting only: turns off general draw batching.
For troubleshooting only. It turns off ImmediatelyFast's general batching of draws and is not recommended for normal play. Needs a restart.
